topics.topic: Required-test coverage of changed and unchanged Customer last-changed instants
questions: Must Required test 11 also show that each Customer change sets the Customer's last-changed instant to the current instant, as A04-3 requires? As written, it demonstrates only the Customer revision half of that invariant.

What must this Required test show about the Customer's last-changed instant when a Customer correction or restriction changes it, and when a Customer correction changes nothing? A04-3 covers both record kinds, but the test states the timestamp result only for the Project.

What Required test must show that a changed Customer's last-changed instant moves to the current instant and that an unchanged Customer's last-changed instant stays unchanged, as required by the revision/instant pair received from State 1?

quotes:
11. A correction that changes a project moves its revision by exactly one and
   sets its last-changed instant to the current instant; a correction that
   changes a Customer, and a mark that restricts it, each move the Customer's
   revision by exactly one; a correction of either that changes nothing
   leaves the revision, and the project's last-changed instant, where they
   were. Shows A04-3, A04-6.

accepted and changed(r) and r keeps a revision   -- A04-3
                          => r.revision' = r.revision + 1
                             and r.last_changed' = now

The revision and the last-changed instant are
  one pair: the revision moves exactly when the last-changed instant moves,
  by the actions listed below, and by nothing else.
judgement.divergence: The stated test permits a changing Customer correction or restriction to move only the revision, and permits a no-op Customer correction to alter the last-changed instant, although A04-3 and the State 1 revision/time pairing require the changing action to set it to now and the no-op to preserve it; the owner reading the Customer observes the difference.
judgement.why: Required test 11 claims to show A04-3 and A04-6 but states the timestamp result only for Projects, leaving the required Customer timestamp outcomes unstated.
options: Extend Required test 11 to require changing Customer corrections and restrictions to set last-changed to the action's current instant and a no-op Customer correction to preserve it.
Add a separate Required tests item stating those Customer timestamp outcomes.
Narrow A04-3 so its last-changed guarantee applies only to Projects.
consequences: The first two options make the Required tests state the full accepted guarantee; narrowing A04-3 would violate State 1's revision-and-time pairing.

topics.topic: Exact accepted-then-replayed sequence required for stale-version owner-action tests
questions: Does “the version before it” mean the version before the already accepted change, used in a later replay, or the version immediately before the owner action itself? The required event order must say that the change is first accepted with the current version and that a subsequent action using that now-stale version is refused.

What exact history must the check repeat for each owner action: must it first perform that action successfully and then retry with the pre-change version, or may any earlier version-moving action create the stale version used to test it?

quotes:
6. Each accepted change of a session — the owner granting a project, revoking
   one, making a project active, clearing the active project, answering a
   request by granting and by declining it, and Kernel replacing its request —
   moves the session's access version by exactly one; each of the owner's
   actions stating the version before it is refused and changes nothing.
   Shows A12-1, A12-2.
owner_action(x, stated v) with v != version(x) => refused, x unchanged   -- A12-1
judgement.why: State 2 already requires every owner-action kind to be refused unchanged when its stated version differs from the current version; whether the check makes that version stale by first executing the same action or by another version-moving action is a factory-check mechanism.
options: For every owner-action kind, accept that action with version v and retry it with v after the version moves.
Move the version with another accepted action, then submit each owner-action kind with the stale version.
Use separate setup histories where repeating the same action would change its legal preconditions.
consequences: Every setup must still demonstrate that each listed owner action with a genuinely stale version is refused and leaves the session unchanged; State 8 chooses the check history appropriate to each action.
judgement.requirement: owner_action(x, stated v) with v != version(x) => refused, x unchanged   -- A12-1

topics.topic: Whether a correction and its audit entry share one UTC clock reading and identical instants
questions: How many UTC wall-clock readings does one accepted correction take when it writes both the record's last-changed instant and A14's audit-entry instant, and must those two stored instants be identical?

For an accepted changing correction that also writes its audit entry, is one UTC wall-clock reading shared by the record's last-changed instant and the audit entry, or are separate readings taken? State 2 must decide how many readings the operation takes.

quotes:
An action has one instant: `operations` reads it from
  `clock.recorded_now` once, when the action's transaction begins, takes
  today's date as that instant's UTC date itself, so the two cannot fall on
  different dates at midnight, and hands both to every module the
  action records a new instant or compares a date in.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged clock-reading and timestamp-sharing question judged in P2: State 3 requires one action instant to be handed to both the corrected record and its AuditEntry.
options: Take one UTC wall-clock reading and reuse it for every instant written by the operation
Take separate readings for the record and audit entry
consequences: The deciding State 3 text selects the first option.

precedent.topic: Clock-reading and timestamp-sharing rules for revision-changing operations
quotes:
An action has one instant: `operations` reads it from
  `clock.recorded_now` once, when the action's transaction begins, takes
  today's date as that instant's UTC date itself, so the two cannot fall on
  different dates at midnight, and hands both to every module the
  action records a new instant or compares a date in.

Every action that changes the store is one transaction `operations` opens
through `store` (A04 rule 4), taking the one write lock when it begins; every
agent-authority call takes it too, a read included (A10 rule 6). Inside it
`operations` reads the action's one instant from `clock`, takes today's date
as that instant's UTC date, and hands both on ("Time"), the record's module writes, and `operations` appends
the one audit entry when the action changed state and M09 lists it (A14
rule 1), naming the release and contract versions, and commits once.
precedent.why: State 3 specifies one clock reading per action and passes the resulting instant to both the changed record and its AuditEntry.
options: Take one UTC wall-clock reading and reuse it for every instant written by the operation
Take separate readings for the record and audit entry
consequences: The deciding State 3 text selects the first option.

questions: The passage must name the compliant path by which the service-to-operations-and-highest-class policy reaches generated code—normally an imported data-provider policy constant, with closed individual vocabularies remaining model enumerations—instead of saying only that Registry knows it from its release.

topics.topic: Outcome and supplied facts for later project creation reusing a preserved request ID
questions: What facts does the later create supply, and must it answer the corrected project as a repeat or be refused as a conflicting reuse of the request id? Merely requiring no second project leaves the required result undecided.

quotes:
A create whose request id such a record carries is
   a repeat when the facts it supplies equal that record's current facts of
   the same kind: Registry answers the record as it stands now and changes
   nothing.

A create whose request id an existing record carries, with facts that
   differ from that record's current ones — a different value, or the record
   corrected since — is refused, and nothing changes; the caller reads the
   record.
judgement.why: The later create answers the corrected project unchanged when it supplies the current facts and is refused when it supplies the original now-different facts; in either case no second project is made.
options: Supply the corrected project's current facts and require the existing project to be answered unchanged.
Supply the original pre-correction facts and require refusal as a conflicting request-id reuse.
consequences: Both cases are already specified, with the supplied facts selecting the outcome.

topics.topic: Treatment of a non-Kernel service call that supplies a session header
questions: For an operation also present in another service's ordinary rights row, what happens when that non-Kernel service supplies a session header: is the header ignored and the ordinary service call checked, or is the call refused as an attempt to use agent authority?

quotes:
The presented token; the operation, one of A09 rule 2's; its inputs, or
that they are not of the wire format; for Kernel, the agent session the
request's envelope names beside the token, never among the operation's
inputs (R0-53).

Stage (1): `service_access.identify_service` and
`service_access.service_may_call`. Stage (2), for Kernel: the registration
checked for the token only (A10 rule 1); every other call through
`agent_sessions.check_agent_call`, a withdrawal's pointer resolved first by
`artifact_pointers.project_of_pointer` — an unknown pointer answered
`not_found` (`agent_call_refused`) without the session's check, the same
answer as any refusal of it (A08 rule 7, A10 rule 3).
judgement.why: State 5 makes the envelope's agent session an input only for Kernel and runs stage (2) only for Kernel, so another service's overlapping ordinary operation is governed by its service rights rather than converted into agent authority by the extra header.
options: Refuse every non-Kernel call carrying the agent-session header.
Ignore the header for non-Kernel services and apply their ordinary operation rights.
Refuse only operations outside the non-Kernel service's row while treating overlapping operations as ordinary calls.
consequences: The later text selects ordinary service-rights processing for non-Kernel callers; a session header does not grant or invoke agent authority.

The review conclusion must be revised or the underlying rules and tests completed first.

topics.topic: Whether project corrections update the project's last-changed instant despite A03's unchanged-instant rule
questions: Does an accepted project correction that changes editable facts change the project's last-changed instant, as A04-3 requires, or leave every instant unchanged, as A03 rule 3 requires? The text must exclude the last-changed instant from A03's unchanged facts while preserving the created instant, or change A04-3.

quotes:
The facts a correction does not edit — identity, status, marks, instants,
   request id — are not part of it and do not change by it.

accepted and changed(r) and r keeps a revision   -- A04-3
                          => r.revision' = r.revision + 1
                             and r.last_changed' = now
judgement.divergence: For the same accepted changing project correction, A03 rule 3 leaves the existing last-changed instant unchanged, while A04-3 replaces it with now; the owner reading the corrected project observes the incompatible results.
judgement.why: A project correction cannot both leave every instant unchanged and set its last-changed instant to the current instant in the same accepted history.
options: Exclude the last-changed instant from A03 rule 3 while preserving the created instant and other written-once instants.
Leave every project instant unchanged on correction and remove A04-3's last-changed guarantee.
consequences: The first option preserves State 1's revision/time pairing; the second contradicts it.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
